column1: # *** THE TOP OF THE WEAR LINE MOVES UP A GENERATION: JOHN WEAR AND ELIZABETH OF NEWINGTON. ***
# Findmypast, England Births & Baptisms 1538-1975, searched 27 September 2026 on David's
# subscription. Row 126 asked for William Wear's parents and said the levers were the Newington
# St Mary baptism register and the 1841 census. THE BAPTISM REGISTER ANSWERS; the census did not.
field
the target
column2: WILLIAM WEAR, born about 1823 at NEWINGTON, SURREY — from his stated age of 48 in the 1871 census and his birthplace as enumerated; a SADLER in 1851 at Salisbury Street, Bermondsey, and a HARNESS MAKER in 1871. He is the top of the Wear line as this archive holds it. Civil registration began in 1837, fourteen years too late to name his father.

column1: the 1841 census was tried first and did not answer
column2: a search of the 1841 census for WILLIAM with surname WEAR and variants, born 1818-1828, in Surrey, returns EIGHT — Clapham, Blechingley, Dorking, Croydon and four at Lambeth. NOT ONE AT NEWINGTON OR WALWORTH. At eighteen he may have been living in as an apprentice rather than with his father, and the 1841 census records neither birthplace nor exact age. The census route is recorded as tried and unhelpful.

column1: # ---------------- *** THE BAPTISM, AND IT NAMES BOTH PARENTS *** ----------------
*** WILLIAM WEAR, BAPTISED 10 APRIL 1833 AT NEWINGTON, SURREY ***
column2: Birth year 1823. FATHER: JOHN WEAR. MOTHER: ELIZABETH. England Births & Baptisms 1538-1975, record R_941493189.

column1: *** AND HE WAS NOT BAPTISED ALONE — THERE ARE THREE SIBLINGS ON THE SAME DAY ***
column2: A ten-year gap between birth and baptism is odd enough to check, and the check explains it. FOUR CHILDREN OF JOHN WEAR WERE BAPTISED AT NEWINGTON ON 10 APRIL 1833: MATILDA born 1820 · WILLIAM born 1823 · THOMAS born 1825 · MARY ANN born 1827. A family bringing its children to the font together, the eldest already thirteen.

column1: the mother is the same across them, which is the test that matters
column2: MATILDA and THOMAS were opened in full and BOTH give father JOHN WEAR and MOTHER ELIZABETH, baptism date 10 April 1833, Newington. Mary Ann's transcript was not opened; she shares father, place and year in the index. SO THIS IS NOT ONE INDEX LINE THAT HAPPENS TO MATCH — it is a household, with consistent spacing of two to three years between births.

column1: and possibly an earlier batch by the same couple
column2: the same search returns ELIZABETH WEAR born 1812, baptised 1819, father John, Newington, and JOHN WEAR born 1817, baptised 1819, father John, Newington. TWO CHILDREN BAPTISED TOGETHER IN 1819, fourteen years before the four of 1833, in the same parish with the same father's forename. IF IT IS THE SAME COUPLE the family runs Elizabeth 1812, John 1817, Matilda 1820, William 1823, Thomas 1825, Mary Ann 1827 — and the eldest daughter carries her mother's name, which is the ordinary practice. NOT ASSERTED: the 1819 pair were not opened and "father John" is not an identification.

column1: # ---------------- WHAT THIS IS NOT, STATED BEFORE ANYBODY LEANS ON IT ----------------
*** IT IS AN INDEX, NOT THE REGISTER ***
column2: the record set is England Births & Baptisms 1538-1975, "Index © IRI, used by permission of FamilySearch Intl" — a transcription of the Newington St Mary register, not an image of it. THE ORIGINAL WOULD GIVE WHAT THIS DOES NOT: the father's OCCUPATION and the family's ABODE, and the exact form of every name. It is at the London Metropolitan Archives and on Findmypast's own London parish images.

column1: *** AND THE OCCUPATION IS EXACTLY WHAT IS MISSING, WHICH IS THE UNTESTED HALF ***
column2: row 126 said it plainly: "THE TRADE IS THE LEVER — harness making ran in this family and a Newington saddler or harness maker with a son William is a narrow target." THE INDEX CARRIES NO TRADE, so the lever this archive nominated has not in fact been pulled. The identification rests on NAME, BIRTH YEAR AND PARISH, all three of which match the 1871 census, AND ON THE SIBLING GROUP. It does not yet rest on the trade, and until the register is read it should not be called closed.

column1: and Newington had more than one Wear family
column2: the same search returns JOHN WEAR born 1825, baptised 1825 at Newington, father JOHN SOUTHEY WEAR — a different man with a distinctive middle name. A PARISH WITH TWO WEAR HOUSEHOLDS IS A PARISH WHERE A FORENAME MATCH IS NOT AN IDENTIFICATION, and it is the reason the sibling group matters more than the single line.

column1: a generation, and four names that did not exist here this morning
column2: JOHN WEAR and ELIZABETH, of Newington in Surrey, with children MATILDA, THOMAS and MARY ANN beside the William this archive already had. IF IT HOLDS, JOHN WEAR IS DERRICK'S 4x-GREAT-GRANDFATHER on the Wear line.

column1: and it does not make the 1871 certificate unnecessary
column2: row 126's other route — the GRO marriage certificate of WILLIAM JOHN WEAR, Q2 1871, St Olave Southwark, vol 1D p.269 — carries a FATHER'S NAME AND OCCUPATION COLUMN filled in by someone who knew him. That would confirm this baptism from the other end, in a document rather than an index, and it remains worth ordering. THE BAPTISM MAKES IT CHEAPER TO INTERPRET, NOT UNNECESSARY.
